the experimental longitudinal sum rule for the lithium isotopes is well described by the calculated sum rule in the cluster models with the exception of the 7Li nucleus.
in the case of 6Li the cluster model is in a satisfactory agreement with experiment while in the case of $ \sp{7}\rm{Li}$ the model is not able to reproduce the experimental data in detail.

in the region between 0.75 and 1.25 fm-1, the experimental longitudinal sum in the 6 Li nucleus is in a good agreement with the theoretical prediction, while the experimental longitudinal sum for the 7Li nucleus is in a poor agreement with the theoretical predictions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in the 7 Li case the cluster structure is not so pronounced as in the 6 Li one, and this fact may be the main reason of the disagreement between experiment and theory.
the longitudinal sum rules in the 6 and 7Li cases are well reproduced by the cluster model.

the experimental longitudinal sums for the 6,7Li cases are in good agreement with the calculated sums in the framework of the cluster models, and this is an indication for the validity of the cluster model in the description of these nuclei.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cluster model with antisymmetrisation performed with respect to all nucleons provides a good description of longitudinal sums in the 6 Li and 7Li case in the high-q region.
the sum rules of the 6Li and the 7Li nuclei can be used for the experimental study of the longitudinal sum rule in 4He.
the longitudinal correlation functions in the 6 and 7Li cases are close to each other and to the $ \a$-particle function.
